readings.mark: dalet: a dot inside the letter at mid-height, read as dagesh (דּ). This is separate from the holam dot, which sits higher, at letter-top height, between the dalet and the first nun.
readings.evidence: The context image fixes this as the word right after זִכְרוֹנֵנוּ and before וְזִכְרוֹן on the יִפָּקֵד וְיִזָּכֵר line, so it is not the later ופקדנו בו לברכה. Reading every glyph: (1) vav with a shuruq dot; (2) pe with a hiriq dot below; (3) qof with a sheva below; (4) dalet with a dot inside it at mid-height; (5) a high dot for holam haser, with no vav letter (spelled defectively, not דוֹ); (6) first nun with tsere below; (7) second nun; (8) final vav with a shuruq dot. That gives 7 letters, ו-פ-ק-ד-נ-נ-ו, with both nuns present. A short vertical stroke under the word, near the qof/dalet, may be a meteg. I can't tell whether it marks a separate sign or is part of the qof's sheva.
readings.confidence: medium-high for the letters, both nuns and the defective holam; medium for the dalet dot being dagesh rather than a slipped holam, because the dot is clearly mid-height but the scan is soft; low for any dagesh in the pe or qof (not resolvable)
